title: CI image builders: every buildx builder runs with the committed BuildKit GC policy, and one made without it is replaced keeping its cache
steps: S1: From the checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap scripts/test/ci-buildx-builder.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code and the result of the cases named in run.tests.
expect: build-app-images.yml and build-dsh-image.yml both create their builder only through .github/actions/buildx-builder.
A builder without the config hash, or with an older one, is removed and created again with the config, and its cache volume is kept; a builder with the current hash is reused.
buildkitd.toml parses and holds the four GC rules: cheap records 7 days, every record 14 days, a 50 GB cap with a 20 % free-disk floor.
evidence: 16/11/2026 dev build host: the builder ran without a buildkitd config and held 98.5 GB of cache (30.6 GB used in the last day, 66 GB unused for 3-14 days); pruning entries older than 7 days freed only 1.47 GB. The runner's buildx is v0.38.1, which takes --buildkitd-config.
fence: Unit cases with a fake docker; a real GC sweep on a CI runner is not part of this case's run.

tests: both image workflows get their builder from the shared action, and only from it
a builder made before the config, or with an older one, is replaced and keeps its cache
a builder with the current config is reused, not recreated
buildkitd.toml is a GC policy BuildKit loads, sized from the 16/11 measurement
